verdict.summary: Slack is self-serve for development and testing, allowing any user to create an app and authorize it instantly via OAuth in development workspaces. However, public distribution through the Slack Marketplace requires mandatory submission guidelines, testing prerequisites, demo videos, and an extensive manual review process.

evidence.note: Slack provides instant self-serve creation for internal/development testing, but requires a rigorous multi-stage review for public Marketplace listing.

wait_days.applies_to: Applies to public distribution and listing in the Slack Marketplace, spanning up to 10 business days for preliminary review and up to 10 weeks for functional review.

evidence.note: Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days (approx 14 calendar days) and functional review takes up to 10 weeks (approx 70 calendar days).

verification.note: preliminary part of the review takes up to 10 business days... functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions

probes.summary: OpenID Connect discovery document found (issuer: https://slack.com).
No RFC 8414 authorization server metadata at 2 candidate location(s).
Authorization endpoint (from docs) responds to a request with a fake client_id (HTTP 200); response mentions an OAuth/client error.
Token endpoint (from docs) is live: an unauthenticated request with a fake code returned OAuth error "invalid_code" (HTTP 200).
Discovery metadata does not advertise a registration_endpoint, so dynamic client registration is likely unsupported.
Metadata does not list code_challenge_methods_supported (PKCE may still be supported; check docs).

limitations: No accounts were created, no forms submitted, no OAuth apps registered, and no credentials were used. Probes are unauthenticated GET requests against public discovery documents, endpoints and documentation pages, plus one unauthenticated POST to the token endpoint with a fake authorization code and a nonexistent client_id (to confirm it answers with an OAuth error).
Review timelines are only marked as sourced when an official provider page states them. Community-reported timelines are labeled as such.
Provider policies change; check the linked sources before relying on a requirement.
